name: Non-linear Diophantine System Obfuscation
description: Replaced the explicit graph independent-set constraint (no two linked nodes can both be selected) with a global equality between two non-linear aggregate metrics (an exponential sum and a linear sum). Because the inequality $3^x - 1 \ge 2x$ holds strictly for all $x \ge 0$, the global sum equality $K = P$ forces the local equality $3^x - 1 = 2x$ for every single link. For $x \in \{0, 1, 2\}$, this local equality holds only for $x \in \{0, 1\}$, thus mathematically prohibiting $x=2$ (both nodes activated). Models that fail to analytically deduce this local exclusion principle will write a generic unpruned combinatorial search that evaluates the metrics and will time out, while models that genuinely reason about the math will recover the Independent Set reduction.
